utterances.text: How long was it before you gave that statement to the Prosecution for this case were you approached, or did you approach them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They approached me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that the same day that you gave them a statement, or was it some time before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was perhaps a day in between. It was very quickly when they found me and established contact with me and I accepted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I said to you that the day that you gave that statement was 5th January 1996, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Before that time were you aware of the case to be brought against Dusko Tadic, that he was to be prosecuted in this court and had been arrested in Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never gave it a thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that he was being put through legal proceedings in Germany before a prosecution against him by this Court was brought about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of all the press that I follow, I only follow the sports. I am not interested in anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, it may be that you are not interested in anything else, but would you agree with me that sometimes you cannot help noticing things that you might not be particularly interested in because they happen to be on the television or they happen to be on the front pages of newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, when you look at a newspaper it may be that it has the front page facing you first of all, and you have to turn to the back pages or whatever part of the newspaper that deals with sport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I use only sports papers, sports press, no other papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had been in Omarska for nearly three months, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From May 30th until August 6th, it is not three months. It is a little less than three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us just call it three months for the sake of convenience.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only exactly, precisely as long I stay there. I never tried to misappropriate anything and you are now trying to misappropriate some days, and days in Omarska were years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and you bear a great deal of hatred to the people who put you in Omarska, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never hated anyone. I even had my best man and those who were God fathers to my child and those who circumcised my child, they were of a different ethnic descent. My best man was Goljan and another best -- and the one who circumcised my child was a Serb, of Serb descent, a pure Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you would listen to the question, the question was of the people who put you in Omarska, not Serbian friends that you may have had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not hate anyone, and my mother did not bring me up to hate anyone. I never saw the police before that day when they took me there. The only contact I have had with the police before that was to get out my ID and a passport. We were a nice family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After you were in Omarska you were also in Trnopolje for about three weeks, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or more accurately not more than 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the four years, three and a half years, after this period of your life, you were aware, were you not, of the news and discussion concerning allegations against Serbians for what had happened in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am telling you once again, that horror is something that I do not follow, I do not watch it, because what we went through in Omarska is worse than any Hitchcock's horror film. I get goose flesh whenever I think of those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So are you saying that you took no interest in these matters if there was a programme about them on television or there was an article in a newspaper about these matters in all that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why would it interest me since I experienced it myself and I know it all only too well? I need no prompters to awaken memories of it in me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you were not interested in all that was being said about what people should do about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have told you, I went through that. I experienced it all on my back, on my head, on my spine, on my toes, from nails to the hair. I have experienced it all and I know it only too well, and I simply do not feel like talking about these things, not even at home, not even with my son who often tells me, "Dad, does your back hurt?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I understand that. But what I ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you do understand it then why do you ask me that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am sorry, but it is my job and my function is to ask you questions about the evidence that you have given and to test its accuracy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, you do your job, do it fairly and honestly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you just would like a moment to collect yourself, please ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is all right. It is all right. I am all right. Just go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now, you said there was an occasion when you were on the pista and a man was identified to you as being Dusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, can you tell me whereabouts on the pista you were at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You want me to show it to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you could stand up and use the pointer and just keep it there for a few seconds so that we can see from over this side of the court where you are pointing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just let me tell you there are no flower tubs here, to avoid any confusion. I was standing, sitting right in the hollow. There was one flower tub and another flower tub and I was here, almost next to the flower tubs in that free space where one could go through and see and back to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I am just interested in one matter as to why you just said to me, "Let me make one thing clear, that there are no flower tubs here"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The flower tubs were there, and that is why I wonder why you had not put them here just to help us with orientation who come here to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you spoken to another witness in this case about flower tubs on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never about anything. If you wish I could approximately tell you how many of them were both on the right and on the left side, and here on this side there were also pillars, concrete ones built into the concrete with chains, and if you think there were no flower tubs there ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you staying in a place at the moment where a previous witness who has given evidence in this case, a Mr. Mesic, is also staying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you had any discussion with any witnesses about the position of flower tubs on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, as regards flower tubs, even if you blindfolded me I could still tell you every single fact about Omarska. Please understand that it is a video tape which we have in our heads and which functions very well. It simply can never be erased. I wish I could erase it so as to sleep peacefully not to wake up three or four times every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told the Court that you were aware of the man called Dusko from the sports pages of Kozarski Vjesnik, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that because you saw -- excuse me, your Honour, I do not know whether there is a problem. Your Honour will forgive me a moment while I take instructions. I was asking you about Kozarski Vjesnik and you said that you were aware of the man called Dusko from the sports pages in that paper, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the sports pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they newspaper articles or a photograph of the man in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On such occasions when it is a question of some more prominent sportsmen, there would always be a photograph accompanying an article, when it came to better, to more prominent athletes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But are you telling us that you saw a photograph of the man who was pointed out to you as Dusko ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- in Kozarski Vjesnik ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- in the sports pages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could tell me if that was on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I noticed it on four, five occasions perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could tell me what period of time this would have been when these photographs were in Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not remember that exactly. I could not really define the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Obviously before June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot tell you. I cannot affirm with certainty anything what was the season of the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, shall we just try? I am not concerned with perhaps the season of the year, but perhaps how long before you were imprisoned in Omarska that you can recollect. Perhaps take the opportunity to think about it before you answer whether it was soon before you had been in Omarska or a few years before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say that, to be more precise about that. Do you remember what you read six or seven years ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What you are clear about, however, is that there would have been a photograph, perhaps published four times, and with that an indication of the name of the person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no doubt about that there was a photograph and there was an article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were on the pista it was someone else called Hrnic who said to you "That's Dusko"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that time you were where you indicated on the pista, were you standing up or sitting down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was sitting down between two flower tubs and the passage was quite clear. The flowers were not kept. It was very hot so that the stalks were very short and flowers faded, perished completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But if you were sitting between the flower tubs there would be no particular problem with you over seeing through the flowers. So the question of whether there are leaves on the flowers is irrelevant, do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not look through the flowers, but through that empty space that was between two flower tubs. I did not look over the flowers or through the flowers, but precisely between, through the empty space which was between two flower tubs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you telling us about the fact of the flowers being without leaf as a way of you trying to make this identification stick?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean? I saw with my own eyes and I am quite certain about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You no doubt in Omarska saw many things over those three months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And what you are telling us about now is an incident of no particular interest to you at the time, nothing was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean of any interest? What do you mean by that? Could you be more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is a man, as you say, coming out of the white house and walking behind the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was moving in front of the white house from the left and turned towards the back of the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he come out of the white house? That is what I understood you to say earlier when you gave your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And went to the left, when coming out he turned left, and then once again turned left behind the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that is it? That is all that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I saw and I only noticed on the right side as he was coming out in that area below the jacket, beneath the jacket, he had something suspended. I could not see whether it is was a pistol or something else. I could simply assume it was a pistol because presumably he would not be carrying anything else on his right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that that was something that took only a few moments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would not say moments. Moments is when you close your eyes and open them, and it went on for about a minute or two, two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He surely did not take a minute or two to walk from the door of the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you trying to be helpful about this matter, sir, because ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why not? I am telling the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But from what you describe would you not agree with me that it is something that would only take a few seconds, five, six, seven seconds to move out of the white house and then walk round the building, around the back and that is you all describe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In five or six seconds you cannot even run round the white house. Let us be clear about that, five, six seconds, I will pay you the trip and take you there and I will try to see you run around the white house in five or six seconds. I lay my hat for that which I brought back from Omarska. So do not ask me such provocative questions. What can you do in three seconds? You cannot drink half a glass of water.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a convenient moment as it is 1 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think it might be. We will stand in recess until 2.30. (1.00 p.m.).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (Luncheon Adjournment) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you like to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged. Witness R, were you also on the pista when a man called Kera was killed by a guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date, but it was in the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you in the same place on the pista that you told us about earlier this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What happened to Kera? Can you describe what took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Mirsad Crnalic, nickname Kera, had been employed in the biscuit factory, Mira Cikota. He had also been an inmate of the Omarska camp like ourselves. On that day he behaved in a strange way. He made strange gestures. We tried to calm him down, to make him sit down, to be quiet, to keep quiet, just to calm him down because we had all experienced the same thing. At one point he started taking off his clothes and started pouring water over himself from a hose attached to a hydrant located behind the hangar in a part which was used as a parking lot. Sometimes he would put on the same clothes, sometimes he would take them off. He poured water over his head. He had some bread that he would not eat normally, so he tried to give the bread to somebody else but nobody would have it. At one point Mira Kvocka came out of the administration building and he happened to be there while Mirso was making those strange gestures and movements. At that point Miro Kvocka said to two guards to take him to the white house and they did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What happened to him at the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the white house he was placed in the first room as you enter the white house on the left, a small room where there had been other prisoners too who also looked horrible. After a short period of time Mirsad opened the door and jumped out the window. Then we heard a short burst of fire from a submachine gun. Then instinctively his head -- we turned our head in the direction of the sound. I turned and I saw Mirso lying down and the young man was holding the gun, his gun at the ready. His name was Mladjo. There were pot marks from bullets on the wall of the white house. After a short period of time there was a command, sit down and face, look down, and that was a very short period of time. I was anxious to, to take it in, so I turned, I slowly turned my head to the left under my armpit and I could see that two or three guards came up to that area, at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So Kera, was he shot by Mlado (sic)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladjo was his name, not Mlado, Mladen or Mlado, but Mladjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mladjo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A younger man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of the people at that scene that you were watching at the white house, did you know anyone else other than Mladjo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot remember exactly all the people because there were three shifts, Krkan's shift, Ckalja's shift and Krle's shift and the worst of the three was Krkan's shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But with Mladjo at the white house when the man Kera was shot, the only name you can give us of someone who was present was Mladjo, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I only saw that individual directly in the face as he trained his rifle, others I could not see because they had their backs turned to me and towards the pista.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No-one else that you could recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. R, first off, where approximately on the pista were you sitting? If you could just stand up and point with the pointer again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you point to it and we need the camera to focus where the witness is pointing, if you can, and keep the image alteration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. It is down a bit. For the record, that would appear to be close to what is the edge of the building, the hangar building, closest to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At most, two and a half metres from the hangar and one metre from flower tub that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could have this photograph -- I apologise it is not on the computer but the technician is not here -- marked as the next exhibit, please? It will be 246. Could you show it to the Defence first, please, and the witness? Could you now place it on the elmo? Mr. R ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like the picture to be brighter, there are some shades, shadows there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I am not sure ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot see the face very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. The question I have for you, sir, is looking at that photograph and, in particular, what is referred to as the flower boxes there ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: -- does that picture provide an accurate representation of how the flower boxes were lined up when you were present in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Does it also represent, give an accurate representation of what the flowers or the plants that were in those boxes liked like while you were there in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that behind where those people are who are in the photograph, is that the general area where you were sitting towards the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, exactly to the right a little bit from where these individuals are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer 246.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 246 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. R, with respect to the incident involving the individual who was identified to you as Dusko in Omarska camp, can you tell this court why it is that you do remember that particular incident? What was it about that identification which causes you to remember it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It sticks in my mind because, as I have already said, the only page of the newspaper that I followed was the sports page, and I connected that immediately with the person I had -- I saw coming out of the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Before you leave that Exhibit, is that the white house that we see in the far right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the corner and the window from which Mirso Kera jumped and got killed. It is the left side of the right house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: For the record, your Honour, this is a still from the video which has already been admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to witness R being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Sir, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. You should remain seated and we will leave the Court room for five or 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, are you going to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Miss Hollis is going to lead the witness, but prior to the witness being brought in, I would offer this as the next Exhibit in order to be marked as 247. Copies have already been provided to the Defence. Exhibit 247 is a two part diagram of the Stari Grad area of Prijedor. I would tender that exhibit, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 247 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The Prosecution call Mr. Huskic to the stand. MR. MEHMEDALIJA HUSKIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, would you please take the oath that is being presented to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Mehmedalija Huskic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on 15th October 1946.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Huskici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you live in the village of Huskici until you were eight years old and then moved to Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you live in Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived there until 24th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What opstina are Huskici and Kamicani in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What years did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to the JNA on 20th -- 28th August 1965.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You served until what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did my military service until 14th February 1967.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were your duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a truck driver.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As a result of your service in the JNA did you become familiar with JNA uniforms, equipment, vehicles and weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could be provided with Defence Exhibit 13, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, I am not sure the interpreters -- are you hearing Mr. Huskic well enough?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, we are, quite well.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could look at that Exhibit for a moment to orient yourself? If that could be put on the overhead projector, please? If you could zoom back out, please? Sir, if you could look at that exhibit and if you could point to the village of Huskici where you were born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the village of Huskici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you point at that again, please? If you could point to the area in Kamicani where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where I lived in Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This area of Kamicani, was there a larger area there that was also known as Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I notice that you put on glasses to review that map. How long have you worn glasses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started wearing glasses a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you wear these glasses for reading only or for far vision as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For reading only.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, how many people lived in this area of Kamicani where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the area of Kamicani there were about 1,000 households, maybe about 4,000 people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know many of the inhabitants of Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was the ethnic group of the inhabitants of Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over 95 per cent Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far was your home from the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My home was about 12 kilometres from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far was your home from the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever go into the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes I used to go three or four days every day, sometimes I went there twice weekly, sometimes once a week, depending on my needs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why would you go into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went there to buy groceries, for I had to buy cigarettes or matches I went to Kozarac. I went to the PA meetings in my school, in my children's school. I went to the marketplace there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you visited Kozarac did you often visit the main business area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the main street in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the homes and businesses along that main street in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the inhabitants of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With some of them I was good friends, others I had met on my way to the marketplace and as I have sold things. There were various ways in which I met these people -- in the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met Dule in the street and we used to see each other in the streets, in cafes, in bars, in restaurants, in various places.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know if Dule Tadic had any businesses in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What business?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a cafe.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever visit that cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where that cafe was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where on Marsala Tita?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter Kozarac and walk along Marsala Tita Street, the cafe was on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any other members of Dule Tadic's family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew his father, his mother, his brothers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Father's name was Ostoja, mother's name Staka, one brother was Mladen, the other Ljubo. His wife was called Mira.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many years did you know Dule Tadic before the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Dule Tadic, I had known Dule Tadic at least 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How often would you see him on an average in a month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes I would see him five or six times, sometimes only once, sometimes twice. It all depended on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you knew him, you knew Dule Tadic as an adult, did you ever see him with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see him clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometimes he was clean shaven, but he was more often with a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there anything noticeable or characteristic about the way that Dule Tadic walked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for instance, his arms would be like this, shoulders bent forwards slightly, slightly bent back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he have his arms out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, like a duck one might say -- not very much, a little.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was Dule Tadic your age, younger or older?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule is younger.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of Dule Tadic and his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, Dule is a Serb and so is his family.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you aware of anyone in the area who looked very much like Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know such individuals.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any other people talk about someone who looked very much like Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the last time you saw Dule Tadic before the attack on Kozarac on 24th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, here and there, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: About how many days or weeks before the attack did you last see Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it could have been some 10 days, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On 24th May 1992 when Kozarac was shelled, were you at home with your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you hear the shelling from where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Two days later on 26th May did you see neighbours fleeing from their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did these neighbours tell you why they were leaving the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because the army was coming from Omarska setting houses on fire, and they had to leave their homes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that date did you flee your home with your wife, your aunt and your son and go to the village of Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is Besici part of a larger area that is referred to as Dera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you remain in this area of Besici until the Friday after the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could again have Defence Exhibit 13 put on the elmo, please? Sir, if you could point out for the Court where it was that you stayed until Friday after the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed in this area here in Besici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time you were in Besici, was that area being shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While were you in Besici did you hear a radio announcement telling all people to go to the Red Cross office in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the announcement say by whose authority this announcement was being made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The announcement came from Serb Radio Prijedor at the orders of Prijedor SDS.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did the announcement tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told to go to Trnopolje and to Prijedor, that nothing would happen to us, that they would disarm those couple of alleged extremists that were there and that we would continue to live as before, that nothing would happen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this Friday after the attack on Kozarac, that Friday morning, do you recall seeing a tank on Marsala Tita Street in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That afternoon did you see men in uniforms come to where you were staying in Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of uniforms were these men wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were camouflage uniforms and the uniforms of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were these men armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did these men in uniform tell you and others in the area to go into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you and the group you were with eventually go to the gas station on the new Prijedor/Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How big was this group that was with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 50 to 60 persons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the gender and the ages of the people in this group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they belonged to different age groups, from boys to adults, to elderly. For instance, there was my aunt who was 85, 86.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ethnic group of these people was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you met at the gas station by other men wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the gas station were women and children put on a bus and then taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That included your wife and your aunt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Later then were you and other men put on a bus and taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was your son taken with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How old was your son at that time?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These buses that this group was put on, were they civilian buses or military buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian buses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the bus company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Auto Transport Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you and the other men were put on these buses, were you taken to a school in the Urije section of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were driven there, were you driven along the new Banja Luka/Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you were taken on this trip did you see any destruction along the route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the houses, not all, but most of them were burnt down. Some of them were destroyed by shells, but most of them had been burned down.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this the houses along the entire route or only along a portion of that route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All along the route from Kozarac toward Koncari.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From Kozarac toward where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the village of Koncari.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After that village, what was the condition of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normal, as before the war, before the beginning, before the shelling began.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of the inhabitants who lived along the route from Kozarac to Koncari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 95/96 per cent were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of the inhabitants of the route from Koncari onward into Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, say, perhaps not 100 per cent, but 98 to 99 per cent were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were at the school in Urije were you eventually put on to another bus and taken to Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any escorts on that bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many escorts did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did this escort wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know this escort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this bus trip from Prijedor to Omarska camp, did this escort beat the men on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the escort saying anything as he was beating the men on this bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did the escort say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he cursed us, mentioning Balija mother, our Muslim mother, our Alija and such like -- all sorts of abusive language he used and swearing.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you arrive at Omarska camp the same day you were taken from Besici, the Friday after the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Omarska I was until 6th August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the guards at Omarska from before you were taken to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Krkan.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a policeman, an active duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in Omarska did you learn the name of the Camp Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Meakic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The guards at Omarska, what did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniforms, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They varied, some wearing camouflage uniforms, some had Yugoslav People's Army uniforms, some had police uniforms and some were wearing civilians clothes as well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What weapons did the guards at Omarska have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Submachine guns, mostly, for the most part, and other rifles and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Omarska do you recall seeing a machine gun set up at a position in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, above the entrance to the restaurant there was a machine gun positioned towards the pista.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other detainees at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the detainees that you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, they were Muslims for the most part. There were some Croats and there were even some Ukrainians.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On your arrival at the Omarska camp, do you recall hearing detainees singing Serbian songs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the songs that they were singing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the most frequent song was "Who says who lies that Serbia is small", but there were also others.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened to you when you arrived at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived at Omarska, they opened the door of the bus and there we got off, to the pista there, and two guards took me and a friend of mine, Ferid Velic, and ordered us to box, the two of us. We hesitated a little, of course, and one of the guards, the one who was behind me, struck me with his rifle in the back and I realised I had to do it, and I began to hit Ferid here around the shoulders, but he was still hesitating. He was quite surprised, what do I know, but then he was hit in the genitals as another guard had kicked him, and then he also began dealing blows to me so that we exchanged several blows and stopped. Then one of the guards told us to go on. The other one said, "Oh, let them be, they are old enough", it was enough. Then we entered a room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken after you had to exchange blows with your friend, Ferid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the small garage.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could take that pointer, please, and point to the building in which the small garage was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What building was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was your son also taken into the garage with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held in this small garage room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there until June 20th, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken after you were held in the small garage room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please take the pointer and touch the building you have just referred to as the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You are talking about the large, long building across from the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this one here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The area between those two buildings, what was that area called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This here was called pista.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were taken to the hangar what room in the hangar were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the last room down there, it was the electric workshop.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this on the ground floor or the first floor of the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could ask the bailiff at this time to please remove from the administration building the roof and the first floor? If I could ask the bailiff also to remove the roof and the first floor of the hangar building? Thank you. Mr. Huskic, what I would ask you to do now, please, after I have explained what I would like you to do, if you would take off your headphones, come around and put on the headphones with the long wire that are on the desk in front of the model, and if you could then show us, first, the room you referred to as the small garage room and tell us the number that is inside that room? If you could please do that now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could go back by the microphone and tell us the number that is in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The garage is No. 1.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you look again, please, at that room? Look again at the number. Is there a letter in front of the number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, A1.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then, sir, if you could go to the hangar building and if you could show us the room you referred to as the electrical workshop room? Sir, is there a number in that room, if you could tell us what that number is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, A17.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If you could take off those headphones and resume your seat? If you could take off those headphones and then resume your seat? Sir, what were the conditions like in the garage, the small garage room, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conditions were not normal.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Tell us what you mean by that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, there were very many of us there in that contained space.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you have any idea how many people were in that room with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 140 to 160.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the other conditions like in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for instance, we could not sit down, all of us. There was no water. The floor was concrete and so on and so forth. It was also hot, too hot.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How hot was it in that room while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, on the ceiling, it was so hot that on the ceiling a kind of fungi began to grow because of this and the paint began to peel off. If you tried to put your hand against the wall, it simply slid down because the paint had all melted because of the high temperature.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that you were unable to get water. During the first day or so that you were there, how much water did you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first day, we were given a litre and a half of water, a Coca Cola bottle, a plastic Coca Cola bottle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was for how many people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I told you 140 to 160 people. At that time there must have been some 150 people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After that first day how much water would you receive on an average?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that we were given a can, a three to five litre can, full of water.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have to do anything in order to receive this water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you have to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had to sing songs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What kind of songs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, again "Who says who lies that Serbia is small" and "From Topola to Ravna Gora" and such like.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any men die while you were in the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the men who died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Armin Gavrilovic called Arko and Adem Beslagic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in this small garage room did you see a man there named Dzemal Deomic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dzemal Deomic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know him from before the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him in this small garage room did he have any wounds or injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had an injury on his back. His spine had been injured by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because it was so crowded I lent against Dzemal Deomic's back and he almost screamed and said,"Well, mind what you are doing", because I was, I heard and I apologised. I said I did not know he had been wounded.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he explain to you how he had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you interrogated while you were at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what building did these interrogations take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the interrogations take place on the ground floor or on the first floor of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the first floor of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who would escort you to the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were escorted for interrogation by guards, camp guards.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the people who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Meakic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met Drago as the Camp Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During these interrogations what did they ask you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked me various questions. For instance, whether I had a rifle, who had a rifle among my neighbours; whether I knew Softic or somebody called Fore or Foric; whether I used to go to the mosque; whence the money to buy a tractor and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons before you were taken to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but not with me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you have, what kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you have that pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I bought a pistol, I wrote an application to the police, I was given a licence, and I bought that pistol because I had a small plot of land and so it was a hobby of mine, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever use that pistol against any Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you tell your interrogators about this pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After telling them about this pistol, do you recall being taken from the camp to your home to get that pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Meakic, Brk, Krle, and two more, I do not know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were Brk and Krle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were guards in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the condition of your home and the other homes around it when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house of my neighbours, one of them was burnt and the other was hit by a shell. My own house was intact, but it was looted, thoroughly looted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there any people left in the area where you had lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that you were taken to your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was about 20th June, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you were taken to your home to get the pistol, did you then return to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you then sent to the electrical workshop room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then how long were you held in this electrical workshop room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there until 4th August '92. Two days before we went to Manjaca they took us out by the dump trucks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time if I could have this photograph marked the next in line which should be Prosecution Exhibit 248 for identification? This is document 19-31. (To the witness): Sir, do you recognise the area that is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What area is that? If you could just tell us generally what that area is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the entrance door to the electric workshop where I stayed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that photograph could please be put on the elmo? I understand that the computer is not working so we will have to use the elmo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the entrance door to the electric workshop where I stayed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, you are pointing to the smaller brown door in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is there a larger door that was also a door to that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the big door that I am showing, but they were never opened.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So there was a big door to the room but the door that you used to enter into the room was the smaller brown door, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: There appears to be a white door to the left of that small brown door. Did that white door open into your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the door, but they did not open into that room. They opened into a room where there were people who worked, who worked on maintaining the camp, maintenance workers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: There is some writing on that white door. Could you tell us what that writing says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says "El" which is short for electrical workshop "Kop".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 248 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to the admission of 248?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 248 will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Huskic, while you were in Omarska camp, did you ever see Dule Tadic there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the day when I was returned from home, I think it was 20th June, when I was taken to get my pistol.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the electrical workshop.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was Dule Tadic when you saw him that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule had come to the workshop.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he actually come into the workshop room that you were in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he do in that room on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule came in, came into the workshop. Someone said that we should stand up and stand at attention. We did so, and stood by the door in two lines. He passed us. He went to the end of the room. He came to a wooden bench and sat down on it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He sat down and stayed there for a while, and used gross language, abused us verbally. Yes, he mentioned Alija's name in a very gross context and insulted us. Then he stood up, walked up to us. He had a pistol in his hand and started hitting us on the head with a pistol. Roughly every second person he hit with the pistol.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When he hit people with the pistol did he say anything to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to some people he did say something, to others he did not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he say to some of the people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came up to Sarejlic and he told him he was a mother fucker and then he said this to Sarejlic and then hit him with a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he do after he went along the line hitting people with the pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went to the door and left, and left the room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time if this document could be marked Prosecution Exhibit 249 for identification and after it is marked if it could be shown to the Defence and then provided to the witness, please? (To the witness): Mr. Huskic, is this a drawing of the layout of the electrical workshop room that was drawn at your request and on your instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead projector, please? Sir, if you could please point to the area that depicts the small brown door you pointed out earlier in the photograph, Prosecution Exhibit 248?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you point to that again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the door.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I note that there are some things drawn inside the room. Could you tell us what those things depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a wooden bench, this is a table, this is another table, this is another wooden bench.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw Dule Tadic that day, what area of this room were you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you were toward the back wall of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that date were you standing facing into the room or facing the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into the room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you standing against the wall or out from the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A little distance from the wall.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there another line of detainees standing in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Standing in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear the question quite well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there another line of detainees standing in front of you or at the back of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Another line was standing behind me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please look at this drawing and put a "W" where you were standing in that room on the day that you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could please point to where Dule Tadic was when you first saw him in that room and if you could please put a "T" at that spot where you first saw him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first saw him in the room, how far away from you was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three or four metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first saw him in the room, was anything or anyone obstructing your view of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did he move to after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went towards this wooden bench.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could please draw a line with an arrow on the end to the bench.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that he sat on the bench. Could you please put a "T1" where he sat on the bench?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As he sat on the bench cursing, how far away was Dule Tadic from you in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About two metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did he move to then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please draw a line with an arrow to that spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then in what direction did he move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please draw a line with an arrow to the last point where you saw Dule Tadic in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic hit you that day while he was in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he stop in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please put a "T2" where he stood in front of you when he hit you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As he stood in front of you and hit you, how far away from you was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About half a metre.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have a clear view of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then would you please put a "T3" at the last position where you saw Dule Tadic in the room that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: About how far away from you was that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 249 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 249, to the admission of 249?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 249 will be admitted. We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Huskic, that day in that room in the hangar building when Dule Tadic stood in front of you and hit you, did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said, "You had a rifle, you had a rifle". Who ever he hit on the head, he said that to him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He hit you on the head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was Dule Tadic wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Other than the pistol that he had, did he have any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had a submachine gun on his back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if he had a beard or was clean shaven on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a small beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "a small beard", do you mean it appeared to be perhaps a few days growth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps a week's growth.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In total during this entire incident, how long did you look at Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that date did you have any doubt in your mind that the man you saw was the Dule Tadic you had known from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not have any doubt at all that it was Dule Tadic. I was absolutely certain that it was Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, would you look around the Court room and see if the Dule Tadic from Kozarac who hit you that day at Omarska is in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please point to him and tell us what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic has a dark suit, a red tie.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is he positioned in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is sitting between two policemen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When Dule Tadic came to your room that day did he have anyone else with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was one man with him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The man with him, what was that man wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was also wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons on him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did that man speak to you or do anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was standing. I did not have my shirt on, only a small leather jacket. He said to me, "Why are you acting like a Tarzan there?" and hit me with his rifle in this area.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that you please note that the witness did make a correct identification of the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will so reflect the identification of the accused by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
