utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Huskic, where were you taken to when you were taken from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to Manjaca, to the Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there until 14th November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken to from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, after you left Bosnia were you eventually reunited with your wife and your son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to the conflict, were you a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you a member of any organised anti-Serb resistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the beginning of the conflict, were you a member of any such organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if we could clarify one prior matter? If the witness could be provided with Prosecution Exhibit 79, please? Sir, if you could take a moment to orient yourself to that exhibit and find the area you referred to as Koncari.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Koncari is about here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if that could be placed on the overhead projector, please? If you could please show the Court the area you meant by Koncari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map) About this area.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please leave the pointer on the new road about the area where Koncari would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you would go up to the new road between Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this is the area.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, are you pointing to the area on the map that is just below the word "Drljaca"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one minute, I am trying to -----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could keep the map just as it is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think I have found it. It had to do with the witness's testimony about his travelling.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: A certain area was all demolished and the rest was not, one was Serb and one was Muslim ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- and I am confused. That is what you are going to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, but let me follow you. I cannot find where he is.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you zoom in on that area again, please, and hold it zoomed in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Is this "KN" -----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Right there, please. Hold that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, I think it is "DRL".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Hold it right there, please. (To the witness): Sir, would you please point to the area again and keep the pointer on the area that you talked about as Koncari? So that is near the area on the map that is marked D-R-L-J-A-C-A, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, was it your testimony earlier that on the trip from Kozarac to Koncari that portion of the route was where you saw the destruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That after that point the buildings appeared normal, in normal condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was it your earlier testimony that from Kozarac to Koncari your understanding of that area was that it was predominantly a Muslim area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That the area after that into Prijedor was predominantly a Serb area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: While we are looking at the map, can I ask a slightly related question? This gentleman, Mr. Huskic, comes from Huskici, am I right? We find that repeated in the case of other names. Besic, for instance, they come from Besici. Does that mean that most inhabitants of Huskici would be called Huskic? Is it the possessive? I take it the "ici", the "i" at the end is the possessive, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Let me ask, sir. (To the witness): Mr. Huskic, the village from which you come is called Huskici, you have testified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did most or all of the inhabitants of that village have the last name of Huskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about half of the village was called "Huskic" and the other half were "Colic".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you know, why was the village named "Huskici"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for instance, I have heard from elders that two brothers arrived in a village, one was called Huska and another one was called Cola, so the village is called Huskici, but half of them were Huskici and the other half were Colici, but that small village was called Huskici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not sure that has answered your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, in your evidence you told the Court that in that electrical or electric workshop, that room, there were about 140 up to 160 people, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say that. I said that in reference to the small garage where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. So how many people were then in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 200, 220 or so -- it varied.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court about the measurements of that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was approximately 12 metres long, six to seven metres wide.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You also testified that not all of you could sit down. It was rather crowded, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You, sir, are confusing the questions. I am talking about the small garage where one could not sit down and now you are referring to the electrical workshop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Again then was the electrical workshop crowded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not as much as the small garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could each of you sit down or sleep on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the electrical workshop, yes, we could all sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could each of you sleep on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, mostly yes -- well, I could not, some five or six of us could not sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did each of you have a special place you were always sitting or lying or standing on the same position, the same place, in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So, I take it that you know who were sitting, standing or lying on the ground near to you, around you, directly around you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you give us names of those who were near to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Kemal Jaskic, Menkovic. There were other guys too. I know some first names, some family names. There was Kemo, I believe he was Mujkanovic, Iso Zenkovic, that was another's name and so on, Paraputic, Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Which Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Midhat Jakupovic -- Midhat Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Any other names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kemal Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: All these people were present when, according to your evidence, Dusko Tadic entered that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So, I take it that all these people had seen the same incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came to that workshop. When I came there, I entered and went to the bottom of that workshop looking for space, for some space. So I reached the end and there was no room for me, and at that moment somebody entered and told us to stand to attention, and Dule came in and then things happened that I told about, and then I went back to the door after that, and that is where I stayed all the time and Kemal Jaskic, Jakupovic were there and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So all the people you mentioned names of today were there when the incident occurred, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were -- those people whose names I mentioned were by the door, and this happened at the other end of the room. That was where I saw Dule Tadic. Omer Mahmuljin, Nadim Mahmuljin were there, Hamdija Hodic and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Did Dusko Tadic openly go into the room? Did he not disguise himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So he went openly into the room, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he openly entered the room, normally without anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was anyone ordered to look at the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not hear such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that others were ordered to leave the room and those orders came from Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How many people were ordered to leave the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that people from the village of Mujkanovici should come out. How many were there of them, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who gave that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there any reason known to you why he gave that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember if a reason was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic came into the room, according to your evidence, openly, without any disguise. You told us that he had a small beard, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In your statement, however, you gave on June last year, 2nd and 8th June last year, you thought, however, that Dusko Tadic was clean shaven. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember giving a statement on 2nd or 8th June ---

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: 7th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- last year. Last year, no, no. It was one year before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Perhaps, your Honour, I show to the witness a statement in his own language?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have only one copy because I did not anticipate it. Could you show it to the Prosecution too, please? (To the witness): Mr. Huskic, would you please look to the front page? Is that your name there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is on the bottom of that page your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not see my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Then I will give you the English version. Mr. Bos or Mr. Usher, could you please show it to the witness? On the bottom of that page do you see your own signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Now could you please look again to your statement in your own language? Could you read the date of the interview for the Court on the first page, on the top page? I am not asking you to read your own statement. I am just asking you to look at the top page and to look at the middle, just below the middle, part of that top page and you will see a date of your interview. Could you read that date, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The witness is not looking at the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The witness is not looking at the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: No, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I see. Would you please look at the last page in your left hand as I see it, or perhaps Mr. Usher, could you pass the top page to the witness, please? Show him which is the top page.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, we would like to determine the date on the statement that you gave. You can look at the one in your language or look at the English version and see if you can locate a date on either of those statements that would indicate to you the date when it was given. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Can you locate a date on the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does it say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 7th August, then 6, 1995, but I do not think that was the date. As a matter of fact, the year is wrong but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Are you sure it says August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 8, there is 7, 8 then 6. I do not know what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does it read "7 8" and then "6 1995"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. From this statement, as you have read the top page now, it seems that you had the interview in June 1995, apparently on 7th or on 8th or both days, do you remember that interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: During that interview you told that the man who came into that room was clean shaven, today you told the Court that he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question was, if Dusko Tadic always had a beard or sometimes was bearded and sometimes clean shaven, and I said that he was clean shaven sometimes and at that time he wore a beard. There must have been some misunderstanding with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, you gave evidence today talking about Dusko Tadic in that room that he had, I quote, "a small beard"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So what is it then, did he have a beard or did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day when I saw him at Omarska he had a short growth, a small beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Today you also witnessed that Dusko Tadic entered that room with one other soldier. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In your statement, that interview you gave last year, you told that, "Dusko Tadic came to our room together with two or three soldiers".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Well, sir, once again on the bottom of that statement is your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So what is it then, did Dusko Tadic enter that room at all or did he not? If he did, with one or with two or three soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule entered that room with one soldier. In that part of the room when he came he was with one soldier. Whether further down the room there were others, I could not see. I showed you how far I could see in that room. That other part of the room down to, down the room, I could not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You also witnessed today that Dusko Tadic while he was in the room had a machine gun on his back. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court how Dusko Tadic managed to sit on that bench you described while the machine gun was on his back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simply he had it over the back. It is a short rifle, so it was all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, I want to go back to the first questions that were asked you by the Prosecution dealing with where you lived. You gave evidence that you sometimes visited Kozarac. You do remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that I visited Kozarac sometimes. I went there regularly. Sometimes I would go day after day after day for three or four days in a row, and sometimes I would be there once a week or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In your evidence you said, "I sometimes visited Kozarac three or four times or twice a week". Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Later on you testified that you would see Dusko Tadic five or six times a day, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not say five or six times a day. Sometimes I would see him two or three times, today once and then tomorrow, another time and then the day after tomorrow. For two or three days, sometimes I would see him every one of those days and sometimes it would be once or whatever times a week. It varied.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could we have Defence Exhibit No. 12, please, on the elmo? There it is. A little bit more, larger, that is what I am asking for, a larger focus, please? That will do. Mr. Huskic, could you look at your screen? Do you recognise what you see there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Do look and familiarise yourself with what you see. Do you recognise the Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to point out on the elmo where the cafe of Dusko Tadic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map) Roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you show on the map where the house of Dusko Tadic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you point out again? Would you keep it on the place where you think it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Dusko's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Huskic, you also gave evidence that you saw Dusko Tadic about 10 days before the attack. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around the restaurant, somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you point to that on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the map).

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We called it "restaurant". It was a Prijedor company. It was a restaurant company. We called it -- everybody called it "restaurant".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. After you came out of the camps, you left the area, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In the country where you live now did you follow what happens in the area after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Practically, no, I cannot watch that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you follow what happened to prosecute those who were indicted as a war criminal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you read about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you seen on television or in newspapers or magazines stories or images of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I watch television I usually watch entertainment programmes. I cannot watch political programmes. I cannot watch movies with violence in them. I cannot read newspapers writing about war reports in Bosnia because that reminds me of my suffering and my ordeal and I do not follow such news.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you usually look to news reels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, mostly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you seen films about the camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not need to see films because I experienced it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, you gave evidence that you were interrogated by a man called Meakic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you remember his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Meakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In your statement during the interview last year, you told you were interrogated by Meakic Zeljko, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Drago Meakic is the uncle of Zeljko Meakic and that is where the confusion came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So who is confused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was confusion. Drago Meakic is the uncle of Zeljko Meakic. I had Zeljko in mind and I said Drago. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So in your interview you were right by saying Zeljko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Today you made a mistake, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was interrogated by Zeljko Meakic. It is possible that I said Drago. It could have been a slip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How did you know that Meakic was Zeljko Meakic? You did not know while he interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zeljko came to the door of the room where I was and introduced himself as Zeljko Meakic, that he was Commander of the camp, that one inmate from that room had bought a pack of cigarettes from a guard and he wanted it back. He did not want any black marketeering. He introduced himself as Zeljko Meakic and as Commander of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Last year, however, you told during your interview that you were interrogated by three men and you later learned that one of them was Meakic Zeljko, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You then told you later learned that one of them was Meakic Zeljko "because I recognised him on TV", do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you speak the truth last year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so. There must have been a mistake, a translation mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Are you seriously saying here there is a translation mistake when you said that you later learned Zeljko Meakic because you recognised him on TV? How could such a mistake occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I did not do the translation. I do not know. I do not know how it came about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that you did see, indeed, TV on what happened in those camps. I suggest to you that, indeed, on that TV you recognised the person that interrogated you as Meakic Zeljko, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Zeljko Meakic took me home in his car for me to get my pistol and I had a good look at him at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In your statement you told that you were interrogated once, and then three days later you were called out again and only on that occasion you told you were interrogated by Meakic, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Zeljko was on his own at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Now, are you interested in sports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Before, let us say, the war in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A long time ago I was interested in the '80s, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you read the Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not lately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In those days, I mean before May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You did not. Have you ever seen a photograph, a picture of Dusko Tadic in any newspaper before May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Before you gave evidence today were you told how the courtroom would look like? Were you shown a map of the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you told where all the parties were placed, that is where the Defence is sitting, where the Prosecution is sitting and where the Judges are sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not told where the parties would sit. Only a map was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you read it on the map, because the names were put on that map, for example, sudija at the place where the Judges sit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was the map marked with, for example, at the bench in front of you, "sudija", that means Judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see the map. I only saw this model. I did not see any map. I just saw this model. No map was shown to me, only these facilities at Omarska. There was no map that was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you were shown in the courtroom itself and shown that model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you expect a defendant to sit on the side of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about where different parties sit. I was not told anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I have one question, however, your Honour, I forgot. If I may proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know a man called Miso Danicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had asked Miss Sutherland to arrange a Prosecution Exhibit made ready in the video room, since the Defence has called into question this witness's familiarity with Kozarac and the business area. I would ask that ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 86?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: 195, I believe, your Honour, which is the video which shows the business street section of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that is available I would ask that it be played and, Mr. Huskic, as it is played I would ask that you identify for the Court the various buildings and structures that are shown on that video.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that ready? While it is getting ready, just for the record, the statement that was marked for identification purposes by the Defence, the statement of the witness in his language is Defence Exhibit 20 and then the English version of that statement which is signed by the witness is Exhibit 20A. Is it ready? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, they are going to show a video. If you could please identify any buildings or structures you recognise as they show this video, please. If you could play that now, please. (The video was played). Is the witness's console on the appropriate channel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the cake shop, the pastry shop, Hasim Pirisic, the pastry shop, the house of Meho Menkovic, of Rejip Kusuran, Brgrad Kolasic. This is the bakery. This is the restaurant. This is the house of Salih Pirca. This is the cafe and the house of Dule Tadic. This is the house of Suljia Mujagic, Fuad Jakupovic. This is the house of Idriz Kusuran, of Edham Hodic, the brothers Hodic. These are houses of the Mujagic family, Idriz Mujagic. This is the house of Meho Memic. Ismed Fazlic's house, Delje and Emima Redzic's house. The fire Brigade hall. The police station. The cafe called Neira. The post office. The cinema. This is the textile shop. The house of Delvic Taric and his father. The old post office. The Garden, a restaurant called Garden, pasta or garden. This is a grocery store, a grocery shop. This is a house owned by the Islamic heritage Vakuf. This is a cemetery where my mother was buried and two of my uncles. This is the Mutnicka mosque with its surrounding cemetery. These are also some graveyards. This is the old school. There is a well in front of the school. The road along Kalate. There used to be two kiosks there. This is the Local Commune office. This is a shop that we used to call a hardware shop. There were flats here. This is a shoe factory Mlesna. These are just flats mostly occupied by teachers. Here there was a bank and some shops and there were flats, residential flats, upstairs. The Kahrimanovic house. This is a shop called Agina Trgovina. This is the house of Meho Memic and his sons. The Mehinic house. The Hase Vuk's house. There was a cafe called Oasis there. House of Muto Dihnic. The house of Hamdija Hodic. This was a residential building. This was a barbers shop here. This was a pharmacy and a textile shop and flats above it. This is the school called Rade Kondic. This is the house of Resad Kulenovic and Meho Kulenovic. This is the old road to Prijedor. This is the old hospital. The house of Bozo Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be enough. Thank you. Mr. Huskic, do you understand the significance of the oath that you took today? Mr. Huskic, do you understand the significance of the oath that you took today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you understand the importance of telling the truth and only the truth as you remember it to these Judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you telling the truth when you testified that in the electrical repair room in Omarska you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was that the Dule Tadic you had known for 20 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you telling the truth to this court when you explained to them your understanding of why there may have been confusion about Drago Meakic and Zeljko Meakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes. Were you telling the truth to this Court when you explained to them why there may have been confusion about the name Drago Meakic and Zeljko Meakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because I knew both of them and that is how it happened, that I confused them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were in that electrical workshop room and you saw Dule Tadic, were there any people in front of you blocking your view of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no one in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is there any doubt in your mind that the man you saw that day was the man you had known for 20 years from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is no doubt whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have additional cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Huskic, as a matter of fact, when you gave evidence you did not say Dule Tadic but Tadic or Dusko Tadic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusan Tadic called Dule, everybody in Kozarac knew him as Dule Tadic. Whether you say Dusan or Dule we always knew who people were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Beside the incident you just testified about today, did you witness any other incident while you were in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What kind of incident do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That someone hit other detainees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was hit by Kvocka, a guard whose last name was Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you witness any other incident where people were hit or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we were coming back from lunch and entering through this door that I pointed out, a guard was standing there. He was dressed in a JNA uniform and he had a police baton and he would be standing at the door and hitting everybody on the back. This is how my wife beats the carpets, the rugs. So, maybe of the 30 of us only two might miss the beatings. But it did not happen every day, but there were many days when it did happen on the way out of the restaurant, the canteen. There was a policeman in police uniform and he kept hitting us in this area with his baton, and when we went to lunch or once to the toilet if you did not, if you were not beaten it was like hitting the jackpot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, do you have additional re-re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Mr. Huskic, you are permanently excused. That means that you are free to leave. We thank you for coming today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let me bring counsel up-to-date regarding other matters that we will be hearing once again because of the limitations that we have on courtroom space. On Tuesday July 23rd we will begin receiving evidence in this case at 10.30 or 11 o'clock because we will have another matters that we will consider at 9.30 a.m. On Wednesday July 24th we will probably conclude the receipt of evidence at 5 p.m. rather than 5.30, because we have another matter we need to begin at 5.30 in this court. Then on Friday, August 2nd we will not hear this matter at all that day, since we have several other motions or several motions to consider in another case. I will remind you again about those dates probably on Friday, but keep that in mind as you plan your testimony. We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (5.26 p.m.).
